EFFECTIVENESS OF INFILTRATION WELLS IN REDUCING FLOOD DISCHARGE AND VOLUME: A GIS-BASED ASSESSMENT IN DALUNG PERMAI RESIDENTIAL AREA, BALI, INDONESIA

Journal: Water Conservation and Management (WCM)
Author: Ni Kadek Astariani, Tri Hayatining Pamungkas, I Putu Riki Ardika
Print ISSN : 2523-5664
Online ISSN : 2523-5672

Doi: 10.26480/wcm.01.2026.449.455

ABSTRACT

Urban flooding in densely developed residential areas is intensified by extensive impervious cover and limited space for distributed stormwater control infrastructure. This study evaluated the modeled effectiveness of infiltration wells in reducing peak discharge and runoff volume in Dalung Permai, Bali, by integrating hydrological analysis, standardized infiltration well design, and GIS based placement. Annual maximum rainfall data from four gauges were subjected to consistency testing, frequency analysis, goodness of fit evaluation, and intensity duration frequency model comparison. Infiltration well requirements were determined in accordance with Indonesian design standards, while GIS was used to identify locations that could accommodate wells by considering topography, land cover, buildings, roads, drainage paths, open space, and setback requirements. The comparison showed that spatial constraints reduced the number of wells that could be implemented relative to the theoretical requirement. The modeled configuration was more effective in reducing cumulative runoff volume than peak discharge, indicating that infiltration wells are best used as a source control and volume management measure rather than as a standalone solution for peak flood reduction. Their implementation should therefore be combined with drainage improvement, temporary detention, regular maintenance, and field monitoring. The study provides a practical planning approach for reconciling hydraulic requirements with spatial constraints in densely developed tropical residential areas.
